name: Versioned Longitudinal Epilepsy Phenotype (VLEP)
summary: An interactive synthetic case shows how an epilepsy profile can change under a newer classification framework while the original evidence stays traceable.
role: Project creator. Designed the research model and directed AI-assisted development of the software and workbench.
problem: A single diagnostic label can hide what was known at a given time and how a reviewer reached a newer interpretation.
implementation: A six-stage pipeline preserves observations in an append-only ledger and resolves a six-dimensional Current-State Epilepsy Profile (CSEP). The workbench exposes the underlying evidence and flags conditional interpretations for review.
evidence: The public workbench loaded. All eight tests for the synthetic Python core passed locally, including deterministic output, ledger integrity and preservation of evidence across framework changes.
limits: The example uses a fictional case. Clinical performance, patient safety and utility have not been established.
next_step: Match the served build to a successfully deployed commit before advertising a release version.

name: GEAR AI CoPilot
summary: A vehicle-owner application that brings garage records, maintenance and vehicle identification into one interface.
role: Designed the vehicle-owner experience and directed development of a cross-platform application and its data services.
problem: Vehicle information is scattered across manuals, maintenance records and separate reference sites.
implementation: The source includes Expo routes for garage, maintenance, chat and diagnostics, an automotive VIN-decoding module and services for retrieving manual information.
evidence: The hosted web entry reached sign-in. The repository contains screens and service code that a reviewer can inspect without an account.
limits: The signed-in workflows and a public app-store release have not been verified. Hardware diagnostics, billing and live valuations need feature-level evidence.
next_step: Record a short walkthrough with fictional vehicle records or build an anonymous preview of one maintenance task.

name: Pool Service Dashboard
summary: A service-business dashboard organizes leads, customers and service records, drawing on the kinds of workflows I managed as a business owner.
role: Independent developer. Connected day-to-day service workflows with a React interface and a Python API.
problem: A service operator needs to see which leads need follow-up and where customer and service information belongs.
implementation: The repository includes lead, customer and dashboard screens alongside FastAPI routes and data models for customers, leads and service records.
evidence: Frontend pages and backend route registration were inspected. The two source links open directly to those components.
limits: A public deployment, customer adoption and end-to-end operation have not been verified.
next_step: Demonstrate a fictional lead moving through the workflow and record the result.

name: EvoChronos
summary: An experimental evolution simulator for comparing runs under different starting conditions and tracking how each result was produced.
role: I designed the research sandbox and directed its AI-assisted implementation with Codex.
problem: When two simulations diverge, a researcher needs to know which inputs changed and whether the original run can be repeated.
implementation: A Rust command-line runner executes the early model. A Python client and HTTP interface provide additional ways to launch runs. A run manifest records the configuration used for an experiment.
evidence: The private development repository contains the runner, client and run documentation. The implementation targets repeatable runs under a pinned build.
limits: The model is experimental. Its outputs have not been validated as predictions of real evolutionary history. The browser interface is at the scaffold stage.
next_step: Publish a small worked example comparing two runs, together with the settings and manifests needed to reproduce them.
